d3e1b5c0-d5d2-4b3c-9b73-b4cf0149e262.one_liner: A distressed/stressed credit PM lays out in granular detail how CLO structural dynamics, disqualified-lender lists, and locked-down post-LME docs are shaping the leveraged loan and high-yield opportunity set into 2029's maturity wall.
d3e1b5c0-d5d2-4b3c-9b73-b4cf0149e262.recap: James Crombie and Negisa Baluku of Bloomberg speak with Austin Camporin, head of special situations at Magnetar Capital (17-year Elliott Management veteran), about the stressed and distressed credit opportunity. Camporin argues the stress universe (debt yielding 10%+) has grown from roughly $400bn to $600bn over the past year even as broad index spreads stay tight, because supply of distressed paper is rising while the buyer base is thinning. He attributes the thin buyer base to three technical factors: disqualified-lender (DQ) lists that block large or 'active' managers from data rooms and voting rights on broadly syndicated loans; scale constraints, since 85-90% of stressed issuers sit in capital structures under $5bn, too small to move the needle for mega-funds; and CLOs' forced-selling dynamic as loans get downgraded from B3 to CCC — notable because B3 loans are now 20-25% of the levered loan universe versus a historical 5-10%, and CLOs hold about 70% of all levered loans. He details Magnetar's process: building LTV-versus-yield regressions to find mispriced 'babies thrown out with the bathwater,' taking ~4-5% tranche positions (enough for a steering-committee seat without needing scale), and hedging long distressed positions with short longer-duration IG credit rather than costly single-name shorts. He discusses sector opportunities (software understood via short duration/enterprise contracts/cash/optionality, building products as cyclical, healthcare services on margin compression from Medicare reimbursement cuts), the roughly $150bn of post-LME 'locked-down' paper as a growing opportunity, and why LMEs are shifting toward more consensual amend-and-extend deals given the $1tn maturity wall through 2029 (half B3-or-lower).
terms: LME -- liability management exchange, an out-of-court debt restructuring/exchange transaction
DQ list -- disqualified lender list, a provision letting a loan sponsor bar named investors from buying or viewing information on a syndicated loan
CLO -- collateralized loan obligation, a securitization vehicle holding a pool of leveraged loans
LTV -- loan-to-value, the ratio of debt to underlying enterprise/asset value
TRS -- total return swap, used here as a way to gain synthetic exposure to a loan without being the registered holder
OC -- overcollateralization, a CLO structural test comparing collateral value to liabilities
steerco -- steering committee, the creditor group that leads negotiations in a restructuring or LME
BDC -- business development company, a vehicle used by private credit funds to lend to companies
